screens.purpose: Establish HEAVY METAL FIGHTING as a corporate broadcast and show Frame scale before the player enters the menus.

layout.background: live service bay with selected Frame in cradle

motion: warning lamps alternate on held cels
one maintenance arm traverses on a low-rate loop
Frame sensor and cooling shutters idle without human breathing
attract mode cuts to short governed demo-fight excerpts after inactivity
antiGeneric: no smooth cinematic fog hiding the title

screens.purpose: Fast arcade navigation over the same living service-bay world.
motion: cursor snaps on a two-cel mechanical latch
selection change triggers one short diagnostic wipe

screens.purpose: Choose the human identity before the machine; portrait character is as important as Frame statistics.
motion: selected portrait changes from select-idle to select-focus
name and affiliation arrive on separate hard wipes
no free-floating full-body animation behind the UI
antiGeneric: no portrait cropping that removes face silhouette

screens.purpose: Choose a Frame independently from the Pilot and communicate size, crew, CORE and doctrine immediately.
motion: hero Frame uses ready/idle held cels or a service-cradle turntable study
stat bars step rather than smoothly tween
Pilot compatibility changes as a hard status latch, not a percentage animation

screens.purpose: Show the Frame as maintained machinery and allow upgrades without destroying chassis identity.
motion: one selected hardpoint flashes with a service lamp
armour plates change only when the equipped module declares a visible variant
antiGeneric: no unexplained attachment floating off the chassis
no upgrade that invalidates animation clearance

screens.purpose: Show Pilot and Frame as equal identities and establish the arena before loading.
motion: portrait and Frame silhouette arrive on different shutters
one rivalry line may type on a two-step bitmap reveal
antiGeneric: no oversized VS glyph covering faces

screens.purpose: Deliver the signature service-cradle, crew check, armour lock and umbilical release ritual.
sequence: crew and Pilot status lamps close in order
cut to arena tunnel ready pose
antiGeneric: no unserviceable cables passing through armour
no identical launch ritual for every Frame

screens.purpose: Prioritise competitive information and communicate CORE as high-output reserve without modern UI clutter.

layout.pilotPortraits: 48x48 at outer ends of structure bars

antiGeneric: crew health is not a permanent second health bar

screens.purpose: Provide a short 90s arcade Overdrive punctuation with animated Pilot identity and no long modern cinematic interruption.

timeline.event: one hard palette flash and stage luminance drop
pilot super-charge cel enters in framed strip
pilot super-call cel and move name rail
pilot super-resolve cel; frame-specific screen field locks
cut-in clears before the real body hero-contact cel; normal simulation presentation resumes

rules: portrait strip occupies no more than one third of screen height
cut-in never covers the opponent for the entire active sequence
body animation and hitbox truth remain visible at contact
move name is separately authored bitmap text, never model-generated text

screens.purpose: Return immediately to the people and machine consequences after the final contact.
antiGeneric: no instant confetti over a crew casualty report

screens.purpose: Resolve the Pilot contract and corporation consequence using cel portraits, broadcast plates and limited full-screen art.

titleIdentity.subtitle: WAR CIRCUIT // 2089
titleIdentity.tagline: PILOT THE FRAME. SURVIVE THE CIRCUIT.

typography.title: custom hand-pixelled display master
rules: uppercase for broadcast and Frame billing
mixed-case reserved for longer dossier copy
no antialiased browser font captured as final art

roleRules: black and steel own most screen area
bone ivory owns primary identity text
hazard red owns destructive or selected states
Pilot and Frame accent colours are local and bounded

steps: campaign loadout and crew confirmation when applicable
rules: Pilot and Frame are equal identity layers
crew requirement and CORE are never hidden
compatibility is status information not a deceptive cosmetic score
same-Frame match retains Pilot and palette readability
retain meaningful collar and clothing anchors
two held states are enough when acting is strong
Frame proportions must match gameplay identity master

superCutIn.rule: The cut-in is punctuation inside a game-authoritative freeze, not a separate cinematic that changes move timing.
